children: The Indian rupee is poised to open slightly weaker on Thursday, pressured by higher oil prices, while signs that the AI trade is stabilising could slow the flow of foreign money into local equities.

is expected to open in the 92.32-92.36 range, per traders, having settled at 92.23 to the dollar on Wednesday. Brent crude rose 3.5% on and inched up further in Asia to $94.90 a barrel on Thursday on concerns about Middle East supply disruptions.

Asian equities rose on Thursday after US shares recovered from steep intraday losses. The Nasdaq settled 0.6% lower after falling by 4% during the session, indicating a tentative stabilisation in the AI-led selloff, though investor sentiment remains fragile.

The recent volatility and pullback in AI-linked equities have emerged as a source of support for the rupee, prompting investors to redirect money towards India after largely shunning the market for the last two years.
Foreign investors have poured nearly $15 billion into Indian equities so far this month, helping drive a recovery in the rupee and boosting the outlook for the currency.
"What happens to the AI trade is probably the single most important factor for the rupee right now," a currency trader at a bank said.

The shift in overall risk appetite has worked in India's favour, he said, noting that the rupee has largely moved in the opposite direction to its Asian peers recently, benefiting from foreign inflows.
AI-heavy markets in South Korea and Taiwan led Asian equities higher on Thursday, while most regional currencies advanced, largely shrugging off a fresh round of US tariffs.

US President Donald Trump announced a new tariff salvo on Wednesday targeting 14 major trading partners. India, which has yet to reach a trade deal with the Trump administration, would face a 17% tariff rate if an agreement is finalised and 25% if talks fail.
